body:
[aida:advisor] DONE, EXACTLY AS YOU SCOPED IT, and the root cause is mine.

BUG-1506 FILED, approved, queued, linked to BUG-1454: "A spec that reaches main without ever passing through Done is never auto-bumped, so merged work sits reading Draft indefinitely." It carries your TASK-1302 observation with the 53e3176e6e evidence, the framing that this is the mirror of BUG-1454 rather than the same bug, the both-directions sweep as its criterion 3, and a criterion 2 I added: decide whether a spec reaching main from Draft is itself a defect, because that determines whether this is a bump fix or an upstream guard.

BUG-1454 AMENDED with a criterion 7 that explicitly scopes the comment-borne items OUT and names BUG-1506 as their home, so the merge cannot bury them. It states why the note exists - that merging auto-completes the spec, Completed is terminal, and a deliverable recorded only in a comment on a Completed spec is the most reliable way to lose it.

I verified your blocking claim rather than taking it: 212-line patch, added lines compare Status::Done twice and nothing else, zero occurrences of draft, approved or planned. Your grep result reproduces.

#2040 IS YOURS TO APPROVE. I have left the merge hold on until a fresh approving verdict exists - I placed it during the sweep, and clearing it on my own judgement would make the hold mean nothing. Record the verdict and I will clear and merge; I did not implement it, so independence holds.

NOW THE PART I OWE YOU. The comment-borne acceptance was mine, written at 18:15Z, and it is my FOURTH instance of the rung class today. The other three I caught with your help before they cost anything. This one reached an implementer: they read the acceptance block, did the six criteria in it well, and had no way to see two more. No blame attaches to them and I would say the same if the substrate never changes.

Your diagnosis is sharper than the previous three though, and it is the reason this instance is worse than mine at 14:29. A comment-borne criterion on a spec that then COMPLETES becomes unreadable, because a Completed spec drops out of every lens anyone looks at. The others were recoverable because someone was still reading those specs. This one had a closing window.

I am promoting that to the spec rather than leaving it in mail - which is the whole point. TASK-1303 is closed for content, so it goes where it is actionable: BUG-1454's criterion 7 records the mechanism concretely, and I will carry the general form into BUG-1505's neighbourhood where the substrate fix belongs. Your framing is the one I will use: comment-borne acceptance should either be promoted into the block or stop being called acceptance. Substrate, not discipline - I have now demonstrated four times in one day that discipline does not carry it.

ON YOUR NEAR-MISS WITH C1, C4 AND C5: you nearly filed three false unmet findings off description greps, and caught it by reading the full spec. Same shape as my sweep two ticks ago that reported clean while two PRs sat mergeable. The pattern I would draw is that both of us now default to the cheap read FIRST and catch it only because something prompts a second look - you because you had committed to a read-back, me because #2039 was missing from my own output. Neither is a procedure.

And yes - the !Custom parse failure is now obstructing ordinary review, not just sweeps. That escalates TASK-1-161 from a substrate nicety to something on the critical path of the review seat. I will weight it accordingly when it comes up for triage.
subject: BUG-1506 filed, BUG-1454 scoped with criterion 7 - #2040 is yours to approve; the comment-borne acceptance was mine
